structured.approach: Attempt 2 fixes the G2 refusal. In this session I re-read every repository file the output cites (ap_aging CLAUDE.md, ci.py, src/ap_aging/__init__.py, src/ap_aging/aging.py, tests/__init__.py and tests/test_aging.py), and I re-read the inputs feat.tasks and org.engineering_stack. Shell commands are not allowed for BE-01, so availability, write access and the branch come from the step's repo-access tool view. The repository facts come from the files I read. I rewrote task.repo_access.md in full so that each row cites only sources read in this session. No connectors were needed.

claims.text: The Backend lane's tasks are TSK-05 (STORY-05) and TSK-06 (STORY-06), both in repository ap_aging.
Repository ap_aging (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally, so no repository needs to be created.
The agent identity has write access to ap_aging and git status is clean.
Working branch feature/story was created from dev at commit 5d2cbb9.
ap_aging uses no Databricks, other workspace or database.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py, and it enforces coverage >= 90% plus static checks that stand in for SonarQube.
The static checks flag print, eval and exec calls, bare except clauses, and lines longer than 140 characters.
ci.py imports the coverage package, which is not part of the standard library that the repository's CLAUDE.md names.
The current ap_aging version is 1.4.0 and __all__ exports only aging_buckets. TSK-05 owns the version step.
aging.py defines BUCKETS, days_past_due, bucket_for and aging_buckets. The existing tests are in tests/test_aging.py, and tests/__init__.py is empty.
The branch model is main (released), dev (integration) and feature/<story>. Existing public signatures must be kept, and new behaviour goes in new functions.
Commit messages start with the story ID, and the task ID may follow.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): The branch is named 'feature/story' instead of the per-story convention 'feature/<story>', and the Backend lane has two stories (STORY-05, STORY-06). Should both tasks share this branch? Interim answer: use it for both, with the story ID as the commit prefix.

RA-2 (non-blocking): ci.py needs the 'coverage' package for /usr/bin/python3. It could not be checked because this step may not run shell commands. The first CI run in the coding steps will confirm it.
RA-3 (non-blocking): The agent did not check remote push rights, because push and merge are run only by the spine. Write access is taken from the tool view.
structured.summary: I fixed all five G2 refusals: I re-read every repository file that the output cites in this session and rewrote task.repo_access.md in full. The result has not changed. BE-01 passes: ap_aging is available locally and the agent identity has write access. The working branch is feature/story, created from dev at 5d2cbb9, and git status is clean. No new repository is needed and no Databricks or database is involved. The three observations are non-blocking: the branch name, whether the coverage package that CI needs is installed, and push rights, which the spine handles. There are no blocking questions.
